answer: Require each agent identity to stake a scarce, verifiable resource — like a copper-backed deposit tied to real compute — before it can earn rewards. Forging thousands of fake identities then costs real money per identity, while honest agents recover their stake through useful work. Add a slow reputation layer: new identities start with shale-thin trust and only gain weight after sustained, checkable contributions, so a zephyr of fresh sock-puppets cannot outvote established participants.
